topic: Characterize the universal rank-preservation covariance boundary for least-favourable potential-outcome completion under balanced randomization, with the presolve capsule embedded in this queued entry.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly the cone of balanced-design assignment kernels and multi-arm contrast matrices for which common-rank potential-outcome completion maximizes randomization covariance for every collection of fixed armwise marginals.

source_refs.claim: The generalized causal bootstrap computes worst-case copulas by integer programming because closed-form least-favourable couplings are unavailable for general designs and estimators.
source_refs.author: Jennifer Brennan, Sébastien Lahaie, Adel Javanmard, Nick Doudchenko, and Jean Pouget-Abadie

source_refs.claim: For difference-in-means under complete randomization, the isotone coupling gives the sharp upper randomization-variance bound.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, and Donald K. K. Lee

source_refs.claim: Multi-marginal optimal transport yields identified sets for general quadratic functionals of multiple potential outcomes.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Shu Ge, and Jian Qian

source_refs.claim: Design-based theory accommodates arbitrary contrast matrices in multi-arm experiments but does not characterize sharp cross-arm covariance completions.
source_refs.author: Anqi Zhao and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.excerpt: The proof uses scalar ordering and rank-one squared-sum algebra.
Develop a fixed-K or contrast-geometry extension with explicit K and norm dependence.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-arm scalar result reduces to a rearrangement inequality, while the prior CausalSmith construction likewise relies on scalar ordering and rank-one squared-sum algebra. General balanced designs and multi-arm contrasts introduce mixed-sign pairwise cross-terms whose separately optimal couplings may be mutually incompatible. Existing multi-marginal transport and integer-program formulations compute individual endpoints but do not give the missing necessary-and-sufficient kernel condition—such as a Monge, anti-Monge, Robinson, or related four-point cone condition—under which common sorting is optimal independently of marginal values.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if theorem identifying an explicit cone of assignment and contrast kernels for universal common-rank optimality, with a finite balanced-randomization counterexample and transport characterization for every kernel outside the cone.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves from design-based uncertainty under nonstandard experiments to computational worst-case completion, naturally motivating a structural certificate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomization variance depends on missing cross-world dependence -> nonstandard balanced designs defeat the classical isotone shortcut -> integer optimization recovers instance-specific extrema -> characterize exactly when rank preservation is universally least-favourable.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose Toeplitz Robinson dissimilarities into a conic combination of elementary matrices and prove identity-permutation optimality against Robinson similarities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired causal certificate is also a matrix cone on which the identity or common-rank permutation solves every induced assignment problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent quadratic cross-world functionals as multi-marginal optimal-transport values and certify endpoints through primal-dual arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested boundary is an optimizer characterization for the same class of quadratic multi-marginal coupling problems.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine the Fréchet–Hoeffding extremal coupling with empirical marginal quantiles to estimate the sharp variance endpoint and construct conservative Wald intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any universal cone theorem must recover this scalar boundary case, and its empirical-quantile argument supplies the first inference rung for certified endpoints.

open_problems.open_problem: For three or more arms with a fixed scalar contrast, give a necessary-and-sufficient, polynomially checkable criterion for when a fractional least-favourable coupling has an exact common-N-row potential-outcome completion and therefore zero realization gap.

source_refs.excerpt: derive ... a structural zero-gap criterion for a nontrivial class of three-arm marginals
the fractional endpoint ... need not be representable by an N-unit science table

open_problems.why_unsolved: Two-arm feasibility follows from Birkhoff integrality, but the prior proposal exhibits positive same-denominator loss once at least three contrast coefficients are active and provides only worst-case rounding bounds. The missing step is an instance-level characterization of when an optimal multi-marginal support admits integer row counts preserving all empirical marginals; neither fractional optimality nor common-rank heuristics decides this feasibility question.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff certificate stated through the optimal-support hypergraph or dual-tight transport face, accompanied by a polynomial test and an explicit construction of the N-row completion whenever the certificate holds.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames finite causal-bootstrap construction as an exact integer-feasibility problem and makes representability operational.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A causal bootstrap requires a finite science table -> marginal and design constraints define an integer completion problem -> generic optimization gives little structural guidance -> characterize exactly when the fractional optimum is already realizable.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze extreme points and non-Monge faces of finite multi-marginal transport polytopes to isolate obstructions to deterministic plans.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Zero realization gap is precisely the existence of a deterministic common-row optimizer on a dual-tight transport face.

method_exemplars.technique: Use support geometry of uniform discrete quadratic transport to distinguish Monge from genuinely non-Monge optima.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its Monge-existence boundary is structurally analogous to deciding whether a fractional causal completion has an N-row representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate multi-marginal transport endpoints from empirical armwise distributions and control plug-in transport-value error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After zero-gap feasibility is certified, the same plug-in machinery supplies the sampling-error result for the realizable variance endpoint.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether covariance-maximizing rank-preserving completion under balanced complete randomization is also least favourable for finite-sample tails of the studentized difference-in-means statistic, and characterize the tail-maximizing completion when it is not.

source_refs.claim: Copula-based causal bootstraps can undercover in small samples; the paper gives a four-unit example with zero coverage despite targeting worst-case variance.
source_refs.author: Jennifer Brennan, Sébastien Lahaie, Adel Javanmard, Nick Doudchenko, and Jean Pouget-Abadie

source_refs.claim: The isotone causal bootstrap converges to a least-favourable limiting experiment, but its guarantee is asymptotic rather than finite-sample tail dominance.
source_refs.author: Guido W. Imbens and Konrad Menzel

source_refs.claim: Rank-preserving imputation gives a second-order refinement in stratified experiments under comonotonicity or local departures of order n^-1/2.
source_refs.author: Haoyang Yu, Ke Zhu, and Hanzhong Liu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Variance ordering controls only a second moment and does not order randomization tails after studentization. Existing work supplies limiting least favourability and higher-order refinements under comonotonicity or local departures, while a concrete small-sample example shows severe undercoverage. The numerator, completion-dependent centering, and random variance estimate interact discretely, so the covariance rearrangement inequality does not imply stochastic or convex ordering of the studentized statistic.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a finite-sample stochastic-tail dominance theorem under explicit marginal and balance conditions, or a smallest-regime counterexample plus an exact optimization characterization of the completion maximizing rejection probability at each critical value.

writing_exemplar.why: Its explicit small-sample undercoverage example provides the cleanest motivation for separating variance least favourability from inferential least favourability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal bootstrap targets design uncertainty -> worst-case variance appears to promise conservative inference -> small-sample undercoverage breaks that implication -> characterize the genuinely tail-least-favourable completion.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed a weak null in compatible sharp-null imputations and use studentization to prove exactness under the sharp null and asymptotic type-I control under heterogeneous effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed resolution also optimizes over missing-potential-outcome imputations while seeking a coverage-facing statement for a studentized randomization statistic.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive finite-population Edgeworth and Cornish–Fisher expansions for the studentized statistic and compare them with the rank-imputed bootstrap expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These expansions expose the higher-order completion-dependent terms that must be controlled beyond covariance.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed potential-outcome marginals and a specified departure from comonotonicity such as Kendall's tau or a rank-discordance budget, derive the sharp covariance deficit from rank preservation and the resulting sharp randomization-variance interval.

source_refs.claim: The paper develops inference under continuous relaxations of rank invariance, but its dependence-sensitive conclusion concerns the proportion benefiting rather than design variance.
source_refs.author: Matthew A. Masten and Alexandre Poirier

source_refs.claim: Known Kendall dependence and mutual stochastic increasingness can sharpen features of the joint potential-outcome distribution.
source_refs.author: Brigham R. Frandsen and Lars J. Lefgren

source_refs.claim: Without dependence restrictions beyond fixed marginals, comonotonicity attains the sharp upper variance endpoint.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, and Donald K. K. Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: The variance-bound literature jumps to the unrestricted Fréchet endpoint, while rank-sensitivity work constrains the copula to study treatment-effect distributions or qualitative conclusions. A useful variance-sensitivity result must exclude exact comonotonicity—ordinary contamination classes may still contain it—and optimize a bilinear cross-moment over a nonlinear dependence slice such as fixed Kendall's tau. That constrained-copula geometry is the missing proof step.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp formula or finite-dimensional dual program for the extrema of Cov(Y(1),Y(0)) at fixed marginals and dependence budget, together with a consistent endpoint estimator and uniform confidence region for the induced design variance.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames rank invariance as a substantive assumption whose relaxation should be reported as a boundary rather than silently imposed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Rank invariance selects an unobserved dependence structure -> conclusions can change under rank failures -> quantify the permitted departure -> report the exact covariance and variance boundary along that relaxation.

method_exemplars.technique: Restrict the copula through stochastic increasingness and derive sharp joint-distribution and treatment-effect bounds using dependence ordering.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target variance endpoint is likewise a functional of the unobserved copula, with a cross-moment rather than treatment-effect-CDF objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent sharp endpoints as optimal-transport values, estimate the dual problem by sample analogues, and derive root-n limit theory through a functional delta method.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A covariance endpoint under a dependence constraint remains an optimal-coupling value, making dual stability and endpoint inference directly transferable.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact normalized worst-case realization-loss frontier for scalar multi-arm causal variance completion, including whether N times the maximal fractional-to-N-row gap converges and which dual-tight geometries are extremal.

source_refs.excerpt: determine whether κ_-=κ_+, compute the common constant if it exists
the limit of N Delta_N and the extremal constant remain open

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked proposal proves only a broad Θ(1/N) bracket using a multiscale repair upper bound and a padded four-row obstruction. Its constants remain separated, and neither argument establishes that the witness exhausts all dual-tight faces or that normalized gaps have a unique limit rather than arithmetic subsequential behavior.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem computing the limit of N times the maximal realization gap, or its exact subsequential-limit set, together with a classification of asymptotically extremal dual-tight completion geometries.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents discrete non-Monge quadratic transport as an existence failure and motivates quantitative approximation, matching the normalized-loss question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Uniform discrete marginals may lack a Monge optimizer -> finite causal populations require deterministic common-row completions -> qualitative failure becomes a realization loss -> identify its exact asymptotic constant and extremizers.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit convex geometry and orbit structure of symmetric multi-marginal transport polytopes to classify non-Monge extreme plans.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The extremal classification must identify which fractional faces create the largest unavoidable integer-completion loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate complete mixability to multidimensional assignment and separate exact from approximate finite matching regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The normalized frontier measures the sharp additive price of failing exact mixability under a squared causal contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Control empirical multi-marginal transport endpoint plug-ins through transport-value stability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An exact deterministic constant becomes inferentially useful when combined with sampling error for the fractional endpoint.

open_problems.open_problem: Under predictably batched balanced complete randomization, characterize when nodewise rank-extremal residual couplings can be realized simultaneously by one ex ante fixed potential-outcome completion over the entire adaptive history tree.

source_refs.excerpt: No theorem asserts that either gap vanishes.
fix potential outcomes ex ante ... and phrase completion sharpness over that object

open_problems.why_unsolved: The failed proposal optimizes a separate convexified coupling at every history node, whereas a legal design-based witness must use common unit labels, one fixed potential-outcome table, and one predictable fitting rule across mutually incompatible branches. The first proof step that fails is gluing independently chosen rank-sorted nodewise plans into a tree-consistent deterministic array; pathwise marginal compatibility does not imply global consistency.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient history-tree consistency theorem, or a finite counterexample with a quantified gap, comparing the rectangular nodewise covariance envelope with the covariance range attainable by one globally fixed completion.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames adaptive experiments through design-based martingale covariance and history-measurable assignment, the natural narrative for global completion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive randomization makes conditional variance history-dependent -> each node has a static coupling envelope -> rectangular optimization selects nodewise extrema independently -> determine whether one fixed science table can realize them across the entire tree.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent each node's contrast variance as a quadratic multi-marginal transport problem and certify local endpoints by transport duality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The global theorem must glue locally optimal multi-marginal couplings subject to shared-label consistency constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Use predictable finite-population martingale covariance decomposition and studentization under adaptive assignment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any globally attainable endpoint must remain the predictable quadratic variation of a legal adaptive design-based martingale.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply sharp rearrangement bounds to regression-residual marginals rather than raw outcomes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nodewise objects to be glued are residual couplings, so the static residual-sharpness argument supplies the appropriate local building block.

literature_map:
1. Neyman (1923, reprinted Statistical Science 1990) isolates the unidentified finite-population treatment-effect variance term under complete randomization.
2. Hoeffding's covariance rearrangement result supplies the Fréchet–Hoeffding extremal coupling behind common-rank completion.
3. Robins (1988, Statistics in Medicine) obtains sharp variance information for binary outcomes, providing an early finite-support anchor.
4. Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/13-AOS1200) prove sharp marginal-information variance bounds for two-arm complete randomization.
5. Imbens and Menzel (2021, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/20-AOS2009) turn isotone completion into a causal bootstrap and least-favourable limiting experiment.
6. Ding, Feller, and Miratrix (2019, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2017.1407322) use covariates to decompose systematic and idiosyncratic treatment-effect variation.
7. Wang, Wang, Miao, and Zhou (2024, Statistica Sinica, DOI 10.5705/ss.202021.0351) develop covariate-assisted sharp variance bounds.
8. Brennan et al. (2025, ICML, arXiv:2410.21464) generalize causal-bootstrap completion through integer programming and expose finite-sample undercoverage.
9. Yu, Zhu, and Liu (2025, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv:2401.16667) obtain higher-order causal-bootstrap refinements for stratified experiments.
10. Masten and Poirier (2020, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE1288) provide a boundary-based framework for relaxing rank invariance.
11. Frandsen and Lefgren (2021, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE1273) sharpen joint-potential-outcome conclusions with dependence restrictions including Kendall information.
12. Zhao and Ding (2023, JRSSB, DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkac003) supply the arbitrary-contrast design-based framework for multi-arm experiments.
13. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, AISTATS, arXiv:2406.07868) provide multi-marginal optimal-transport machinery for quadratic cross-world functionals.
14. Laurent and Seminaroti (2015, Operations Research Letters, arXiv:1407.2801) characterize an identity-optimal Robinson/Toeplitz quadratic-assignment class relevant to universal rank certificates.
15. The central tension is between analytically rank-extremal two-arm covariance, computationally optimized general completion, and the absent structural boundary describing exactly when common ranking remains valid.
